datasets.title: Geodata of Damage Assessment of Chitral Area, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province, Pakistan
datasets.description: This map illustrates satellite-detected damage and destruction in the Chitral area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province, Pakistan, and located roughly 120 km southwest of the 26 October 2015 earthquake epicenter. Using a Pléiades satellite image acquired 31 October 2015 and a WorldView-2 image acquired 12 August 2015, UNITAR/UNOSAT identified 369 potentially damaged structures. Some areas could not be analyzed because of the cloud coverage on the reference image. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to UNITAR/UNOSAT.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/geodata-of-damage-assessment-of-chitral-area-khyber-pakhtunkhwa-province-paki-november-03-2015]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts compared Pléiades satellite imagery acquired 31 October 2015 (post-event) with WorldView-2 reference imagery from 12 August 2015 (pre-event) to detect structural damage in the Chitral area through visual change detection. The analysis identified 369 potentially damaged structures but was preliminary and not field-validated.

sources.name: United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Satellite-based damage assessment using Pléiades and WorldView-2 imagery acquired before and after the earthquake to identify potentially damaged structures through change detection analysis.
